summary.en-US: Per-page request firewall with geoip, geosite, sing-box rule-set, domain regex, and IP range rules

description.en-US:
GeoLock is a Firefox extension that blocks or allows requests with per-page rules: geoip country, geosite category, sing-box rule-sets, domain regex, and IP ranges.

How it works

Every time a page loads something — a script, an image, an API call — GeoLock checks your rules and lets it through or stops it.

A rule pairs a source (the page making the request) with a destination (what it's loading). If both match, the rule fires with its action: allow or block.

Rules run top to bottom. The first match wins. If nothing matches, your default action applies.

Example rules:

• When on a US site, block resources resolving to non-US IPs
• Allow only known CDNs on a sensitive site
• Block all traffic between two countries with one isolate rule

Matchers

• geoip — country of the resolved IP (v2fly geoip.dat)
• geosite — domain category like google, category-ads-all (v2fly geosite.dat)
• ruleset — sing-box rule-set, binary .srs or JSON source format
• domain — regex against the hostname
• url — regex against the full URL
• ip — CIDR range, IPv4 or IPv6
• any — matches everything
• and / or / not — combine the above

Features

• Bidirectional rules — fire in both source↔destination directions
• Isolate rules — define one boundary (say, "US") and fire whenever traffic crosses it
• Data sources by URL — geoip/geosite databases and any number of named sing-box rule-sets, auto-updated on a schedule
• Remote configuration — fetch and apply your config from a URL
• Built-in rule tester, per-page block log with match traces
• Raw JSON editor, import/export, one-click reset
• In-memory DNS cache, no telemetry

Source: https://github.com/mazzz1y/geolock

version.approval_notes:
Build: npm ci && npm run build. Plain ES modules, no bundler or minification. Tests: node tests/run.mjs (all unit tests passing).

Permissions:
- webRequest + webRequestBlocking: required to inspect and cancel sub-resource requests as the rules engine matches them.
- webNavigation: required to associate sub-resource requests with the originating page (frame tracking).
- host_permissions <all_urls>: required because the firewall must see every outgoing request to apply rules; cannot be narrowed without losing core functionality.
- dns: used to resolve hostnames for geoip/ip matchers; lookups are local to the browser.
- storage, alarms: configuration persistence and scheduled geo-data updates.

No telemetry, no analytics, no remote code. data_collection_permissions is set to ["none"] in manifest.json. Geo databases are fetched from user-configured HTTPS URLs at runtime; no databases are bundled.

Android: gecko_android.strict_min_version is 142.0 in manifest.json (matches desktop floor). MV3 background scripts (event-page style) are used; no service workers.
